name: Sham litigation, arbitration and legal settlements used to launder or justify funds
description: Criminals use real or invented legal disputes, arbitration awards, court judgments or settlements to move money and to give it a documented, apparently lawful origin. The parties are typically connected, the claim has little commercial substance and the payout follows quickly. Lawyers, escrow and client accounts, and receiving banks are the main exposure points.

sources.text: FATF, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Vulnerabilities of Legal Professionals, 2013

exposure.rationale: Law-firm client and escrow accounts and receiving banks handle settlement and award payouts between related parties; wire-based.

indicators.name: Rapid cash-out of settlements to third-party accounts
indicators.canon: Rapid cash-out of settlements to third-party accounts
indicators.desc: Settlement funds are sent immediately to unrelated accounts, often offshore.
indicators.ctx: Award or settlement money is sent on straight away to third-party or offshore accounts rather than kept by the claimant.

indicators.name: Professional client account used as pass-through
indicators.canon: Professional client account used as pass-through
indicators.desc: A professional's client account is used to move funds with no underlying legal or advisory work.
indicators.ctx: A law firm's client account receives and then pays out settlement funds with little genuine legal work behind the flow.

indicators.name: Client or pooled accounts used for non-client flows
indicators.canon: Client or pooled accounts used for non-client flows
indicators.desc: Professionals' client accounts used as banks.
indicators.ctx: Client or escrow accounts hold and release dispute funds as if they were a bank account for the parties.

indicators.name: Fee arrangements disproportionate to services or paid by third parties
indicators.canon: Fee arrangements disproportionate to services or paid by third parties
indicators.ctx: Legal or arbitration fees that are very high, success-based without any contest, or paid by a party outside the matter.

indicators.name: Professional's role unusual for the work
indicators.canon: Professional's role unusual for the work
indicators.desc: Professional acts as nominee, director, or intermediary beyond normal remit.
indicators.ctx: A lawyer or intermediary acts as paying agent, escrow or nominee in a way that goes beyond the stated dispute.

indicators.name: Auction or intermediary used to obscure parties
indicators.canon: Auction or intermediary used to obscure parties
indicators.ctx: Court-ordered or contrived forced-sale and auction processes with agents or anonymous bidders hide who actually acquires the asset.

indicators.name: Inconsistent loan documentation or backdated agreements
indicators.canon: Inconsistent loan documentation or backdated agreements
indicators.ctx: The contract, loan or invoice underlying the claim is backdated, inconsistent or appears prepared after the dispute arose.

indicators.name: Dispute or award between related parties resolved quickly without contest
indicators.canon: Dispute or award between related parties resolved quickly without contest
indicators.desc: A claim, arbitration or judgment is brought between parties that are linked by ownership, control, address or advisers, and it ends in a consent order, uncontested default or quick award with immediate payment.
indicators.ctx: Strongest sign that the legal process is a vehicle rather than a real dispute.
indicators.fp: Group companies, family firms and joint ventures genuinely settle intra-group disputes, and early settlement is common. Check for a real commercial history and whether other group entities are also paid.

indicators.name: Settlement or award funded by a party with no link to the dispute
indicators.canon: Settlement or award funded by a party with no link to the dispute
indicators.desc: The payment of a settlement or judgment comes from an unrelated third party, a newly created entity or an offshore account instead of the named respondent.
indicators.ctx: Source-of-funds red flag on the receiving side, as the payer's identity does not match the legal record.
indicators.fp: Insurers, guarantors, parent companies and liability funds may legitimately pay on behalf of a respondent. Obtain the documentary basis for the payer.

indicators.name: Claim with no commercial basis or prior trading history
indicators.canon: Claim with no commercial basis or prior trading history
indicators.desc: The legal claim rests on a contract, service or loss that lacks supporting commercial evidence, a trading history between the parties, or a plausible amount in relation to the stated losses.
indicators.ctx: Helps separate a genuine though weak dispute from a fabricated one.
indicators.fp: Early-stage claims may be thinly evidenced and some disputes are about informal deals. Corroborate with counterparties or independent records.

added.subject: Add 9 typologies from reference review (market abuse, complicit FI, sham legal, sports, freeports, pensions, transfer pricing, scam compounds, cross-border mules)
